cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Merciful Lie
cards.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. The bakery can't sell your cake, love. They think it's too special to slice. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says 'inedible.' I thought I'd finally found something I was good at.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. You have. Display cakes aren't meant to be eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll ask them to put it in the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me ask. I'll explain the display concept before they get confused again.

mechanism: A protects B from painful rejection by confidently managing an alternative explanation, then accepting B conditions to keep trust and participation alive.
confusable: Distinguish genuine neutral reinterpretation from a clearly protective false account under pressure from rejection evidence and B threatened self-belief.
comparison: Cake rejection becomes display-category opportunity; poem return becomes space/booklet opportunity with A public endorsement demanded.
seedUse: Canonical bakery and poem seeds have explicit hurt stakes; retain their protective causality while making S02 accommodation part of how the lie is maintained.
